```text
1	# marvin-perf
2	
3	Host-side decoder and analyzer for the marvin firmware **perf-log** wire format.
4	
5	The firmware emits framed binary records (schema version 1) over its USB-device
6	CDC ACM port. This tool consumes that stream live, records it to disk, replays
7	captures offline, and produces summary analyses (latency attribution, drop
8	accounting, stack high-water trends).
9	
10	Wire format source-of-truth lives in the firmware tree at
11	[`firmware/marvin/default/src/perf_log/perf_log_records.h`](../../firmware/marvin/default/src/perf_log/perf_log_records.h).
12	The Python schema mirror in [`marvin_perf/records.py`](marvin_perf/records.py)
13	must match it byte-for-byte; bump `PERF_LOG_SCHEMA_VERSION` on both sides
14	together.
15	
16	## Setup
17	
18	All Python work runs through [**uv**](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/). First-time
19	bootstrap:
20	
21	    cd tools/marvin-perf
22	    uv sync
23	
24	`uv sync` creates `.venv/` and writes `uv.lock`. Subsequent invocations use the
25	existing venv automatically.
26	
27	## Usage
28	
29	    # Live decode from the marvin USB-device CDC port
30	    uv run marvin-perf live --port /dev/cu.usbmodem...
31	
32	    # Live decode and capture raw bytes to disk in parallel
33	    uv run marvin-perf live --port /dev/cu.usbmodem... --also-record session.bin
34	
35	    # Capture raw bytes only (no decode)
36	    uv run marvin-perf record --port /dev/cu.usbmodem... --out session.bin
37	
38	    # Pretty-print every record in a captured file
39	    uv run marvin-perf decode session.bin
40	
41	    # Run the full analysis pass over a captured file
42	    uv run marvin-perf summarize session.bin
43	
44	## Tests
45	
46	    uv run pytest
47	
48	Fixtures under [`tests/fixtures/`](tests/fixtures/) are hand-built byte streams
49	covering one frame per record type plus framing edge cases (FCS mismatch,
50	truncated payload, mid-stream join needing SOF resync).
51
```
</details></tool-use>

8	/* Perf-log wire format. Mirror this header byte-for-byte in the host
9	 * decoder (tools/marvin-perf). Bump PERF_LOG_SCHEMA_VERSION on
10	 * every layout change; the host refuses streams that don't match.
11	 *
12	 * All fields little-endian, naturally aligned, fixed width. Records
13	 * are framed on the wire by the drain task (SOF magic + length + CRC);
14	 * the structs below are the framed payload only. */
15	
16	#define PERF_LOG_SCHEMA_VERSION   2u
17	
18	#define PERF_LOG_HDR_MAGIC        0x4D56u   /* 'M','V' little-endian */
19	
20	/* SOF bytes: 0x55 0x4D 0x52 0x56 ("UMRV"). Distinct from the 16-bit
21	 * header magic so a mid-stream reader can resync on a 4-byte pattern. */
22	#define PERF_LOG_SOF_0            0x55u
23	#define PERF_LOG_SOF_1            0x4Du
24	#define PERF_LOG_SOF_2            0x52u
25	#define PERF_LOG_SOF_3            0x56u
26	
27	typedef enum

29	    PERF_REC_SESSION        = 0x01,
30	    PERF_REC_STAMP          = 0x02,
31	    PERF_REC_DETECTOR       = 0x03,
32	    PERF_REC_TIMING         = 0x04,
33	    PERF_REC_STRIP          = 0x05,
34	    PERF_REC_DROP           = 0x06,
35	    PERF_REC_TASK_HIGHWATER = 0x07,
36	    PERF_REC_TASK_RUNTIME   = 0x08,
37	} perf_rec_type_t;
38	
39	/* stage_id values for PERF_REC_STAMP. Producer call sites map 1:1. */
40	typedef enum
41	{
42	    PERF_STAGE_ISC_IRQ            = 0x10,
43	    PERF_STAGE_VIDEO_PUBLISH      = 0x11,
44	    PERF_STAGE_CV_START           = 0x20,
45	    PERF_STAGE_CV_END             = 0x21,
46	    PERF_STAGE_TP_TICK            = 0x30,
47	    PERF_STAGE_FBL_SEND           = 0x40,
48	    PERF_STAGE_CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE = 0x41,
49	} perf_stage_t;
50

55	{

57	    uint8_t  type;            /* perf_rec_type_t */
58	    uint8_t  flags;           /* PERF_FLAG_* */
59	    uint32_t frame_epoch;     /* Video_FrameInfo.frame_count at producer site */
60	    uint64_t ts_counter;      /* SYS_TIME raw counter; host divides by timer_freq_hz */

63	/* PERF_REC_SESSION — emitted once when the drain task starts. The host
64	 * decoder uses timer_freq_hz to convert ts_counter to seconds and

66	typedef struct __attribute__((packed))
67	{
68	    perf_hdr_t hdr;

77	 *   ISC_IRQ           : reserved (0)
78	 *   VIDEO_PUBLISH     : subscriber bitmask
79	 *   CV_START / CV_END : reserved (0)
80	 *   TP_TICK           : publish_mask (low 7 bits)
81	 *   FBL_SEND          : queued mask
82	 *   CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE: USB CDC result code */
83	typedef struct __attribute__((packed))
84	{
85	    perf_hdr_t hdr;

87	    uint8_t    reserved[3];
88	    uint32_t   aux;

97	typedef struct __attribute__((packed))

100	    uint16_t   hold_dist[FRET_COUNT];   /* 5 × 2 = 10 B */
101	    uint16_t   edge_dist[FRET_COUNT];   /* 5 × 2 = 10 B */

125	    uint32_t   dropped_state;
126	    uint32_t   dropped_strip;
127	    uint32_t   dropped_sink;

129	} perf_rec_drop_t;

132	 * a stable enum mirrored in the host decoder; words is the
133	 * uxTaskGetStackHighWaterMark return (StackType_t units). */
134	typedef enum
135	{
136	    PERF_TASK_VIDEO          = 0,
137	    PERF_TASK_CV_MARVIN_V1   = 1,
138	    PERF_TASK_DETECTOR_DRAIN = 2,
139	    PERF_TASK_TIMING         = 3,
140	    PERF_TASK_FRETBOARD_LINK = 4,
141	    PERF_TASK_PERF_DRAIN     = 5,
142	} perf_task_id_t;
143	
144	typedef struct __attribute__((packed))
145	{
146	    perf_hdr_t hdr;
147	    uint8_t    task_id;
148	    uint8_t    reserved[3];
149	    uint32_t   words;
150	} perf_rec_task_highwater_t;
151	
152	/* PERF_REC_STRIP — variable-size BGR888 region of interest, kind-tagged.
153	 * Today's producers emit SENSING (row through the sensor patches) and
154	 * STRIKE (row through the strum trigger zone), each 240×32 once per ISC
155	 * frame. Future kinds (SCORE, MINIMAP, etc.) plug into the same record
156	 * type — adding one is an enum entry plus a producer; no schema bump.
157	 *
158	 * Wire payload size is HDR + 12 B body + w*h*PERF_STRIP_BPP bytes,
159	 * tightly packed. The queue slot is sized to PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES; the
160	 * drain task computes the on-wire length from (w, h) and frames only
161	 * what's used. */
162	typedef enum
163	{
164	    PERF_STRIP_SENSING = 0,
165	    PERF_STRIP_STRIKE  = 1,
166	} perf_strip_kind_t;
167	
168	#define PERF_STRIP_BPP        3u
169	
170	/* Wire-bound on the strip pixel-data size. Two stacked caps determine
171	 * the maximum payload a strip can carry:
172	 *
173	 *   1. Wire LEN field is u16 → max payload 65535 bytes
174	 *      → max pixel = 65535 − HDR(16) − BODY(12) = 65507
175	 *   2. UDPHS DMA single-transfer cap is
176	 *      DRV_USB_UDPHS_DMA_MAX_TRANSFER_SIZE × 64 KB
177	 *      (currently 2 × 64 KB = 128 KB; well above the LEN cap)
178	 *
179	 * The u16 LEN field is the binding constraint. Set at 65000 to land just
180	 * under it with a small margin. Producers may use any (w, h) shape as
181	 * long as w * h * PERF_STRIP_BPP <= PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES.
182	 *
183	 * Practical strip-size envelope (pixel area = w*h ≤ ~21666):
184	 *   720×30  640×33  480×45  320×64  290×72
185	 *
186	 * Buffer footprint scales with this:
187	 *   pool      = PL_STRIP_POOL_SIZE × (28 + PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES)
188	 *   sink ring = SINK_TX_RING_DEPTH × round_up_64(36 + PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES)
189	 * Together ~585 KB BSS at 65000; trivially fits in the 240 MB cached DDR.
190	 *
191	 * To go beyond u16 LEN, the wire format itself needs a schema break (LEN
192	 * → u32). Don't do that lightly — at 60 fps × 65 KB = ~3.9 MB/s, this cap
193	 * already lines up with what the wire can sustainably carry. */
194	#define PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES  65000u
195	
196	#define PERF_STRIP_HDR_BYTES  (sizeof(perf_hdr_t) + 12u)   /* hdr + body */
197	
198	typedef struct __attribute__((packed))
199	{
200	    perf_hdr_t hdr;
201	    uint16_t   x, y;          /* top-left in source frame */
202	    uint16_t   w, h;          /* per-record dimensions */
203	    uint8_t    kind;          /* perf_strip_kind_t */
204	    uint8_t    reserved[3];
205	    uint8_t    bgr[PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES];   /* sized to max in queue slot */
206	} perf_rec_strip_t;
207

209	 * cumulative run-time counter. Drain task emits one record per known
210	 * task at 1 Hz alongside DROP and TASK_HIGHWATER. Host computes per-
211	 * window CPU% as Δrun_time_counter[task] / ΣΔrun_time_counter. */
212	typedef enum
213	{
214	    PERF_TASK_STATE_RUNNING   = 0,
215	    PERF_TASK_STATE_READY     = 1,
216	    PERF_TASK_STATE_BLOCKED   = 2,
217	    PERF_TASK_STATE_SUSPENDED = 3,
218	    PERF_TASK_STATE_DELETED   = 4,
219	    PERF_TASK_STATE_INVALID   = 5,
220	} perf_task_state_t;
221	
222	typedef struct __attribute__((packed))
223	{
224	    perf_hdr_t hdr;
225	    uint8_t    task_id;            /* perf_task_id_t */
226	    uint8_t    state;              /* perf_task_state_t (mirrors eTaskState) */
227	    uint8_t    priority;           /* uxCurrentPriority */
228	    uint8_t    reserved;
229	    uint32_t   run_time_counter;   /* low 32 bits of ulRunTimeCounter */
230	    uint32_t   reserved2;
231	} perf_rec_task_runtime_t;
232

238	 * endpoint; the host writes them via marvin-perf's set-mask path. */
239

241	
242	typedef enum

245	} perf_cmd_t;

1	# marvin — Working Journal
2	
3	Running log of planning, decisions, open questions, and work-in-progress for marvin. Newest entries at the top. For *what marvin is* (purpose, subsystems, interfaces, milestones), read [`spec.md`](spec.md) — this journal does not duplicate it.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## Current focus
8	
9	**M1 — Reference detector v0.** First CV detector running on captured frames, publishing `detector_state_t` records onto the detector-state bus. No actuation yet. See [`spec.md`](spec.md) §4.2 for subsystem detail and §8 for the milestone progression.
10	
11	Scaffold is in place as of 2026-05-20: `detector/detector.{h,c}` owns the bus queue + a temporary drain task that logs records-per-second; `detector/cv_marvin_v1.{h,c}` subscribes to the video frame queue and publishes one `detector_state_t` per frame with `frame_epoch = Video_FrameInfo.frame_count` and all-zero fret state. Next: pick the v0 algorithm (Q8) and start populating `fret[]`.
12	
13	**Capture/display pipeline is done as of 2026-05-02:** source → TC358743 → CSI-2 @ 972 Mbps/lane → SAM9X75 → ISC DMA → DDR (BGRX32) → XLCDC OVR1 → LVDSC → 10.1″ 1280×800 LVDS panel.
14	
15	> **Deeper-dive references:**
16	> - [`spec.md`](spec.md) — system-level spec (read first).
17	> - [`capture_pipeline.md`](capture_pipeline.md) — HDMI → DDR capture stage (CSI2DC, ISC, register settings, datasheet citations).
18	> - [`display_path.md`](display_path.md) — DDR → LCD display stage (XLCDC OVR1 wiring, pillarbox, cache coherence).
19	
20	> **Earlier entries** (capture/display bring-up, 2026-05-01 → 2026-05-15) are preserved in [`journal-archive.md`](journal-archive.md).
21	
22	---
23	
24	## Decision log
25	
26	| Date | Decision | Rationale |
27	|------|----------|-----------|
28	| 2026-05-29 | Patch the UDPHS device driver to arm DMA for queued IRPs in completion ISRs. New helper `F_DRV_USB_UDPHS_DEVICE_ArmDmaForIrp` called after queue advance in `Tasks_ISR_DMA` and the ZLP-completion path. Logged as patch #9. | Stock Harmony USB v3.16.0 driver only programs the DMA channel in `IRPSubmit`'s queue-empty branch — IRPs appended to a non-empty queue link in the linked list but never get armed for transmission. Without this, `queueSizeWrite > 1` accepts writes but only ever transmits the first of any batch — we'd accept three perf-log strips, transmit one, the other two stranded forever. The IRP-queue infrastructure is *already there* in the driver, the missing piece is the post-completion arm. Fix is additive (new helper, two new call sites, no refactor of existing IRPSubmit body), making it easy to find/maintain after MCC regen. Future Harmony versions may obviate this if upstream wires it up. |

117	     ```c
118	     extern uint64_t SYS_TIME_Counter64Get(void);
119	     #define configRUN_TIME_COUNTER_TYPE             uint64_t
120	     #define portCONFIGURE_TIMER_FOR_RUN_TIME_STATS()
121	     #define portGET_RUN_TIME_COUNTER_VALUE()        SYS_TIME_Counter64Get()
122	     ```
123	     `SYS_TIME` is already initialised by Harmony before the scheduler starts, so the configure macro is a no-op. `SYS_TIME_Counter64Get` returns the full 64-bit TC0 CH0 counter; the matching `configRUN_TIME_COUNTER_TYPE = uint64_t` overrides FreeRTOS's `uint32_t` default so cumulative `ulRunTimeCounter` values don't wrap (uint32_t at 266 MHz wraps after ~16 s of accumulated CPU time across all tasks, which made percentages garbage almost immediately). 180	**Multi-IRP pipelining via UDPHS driver patch.** The journal's "lever 1" hypothesis (pipeline CDC writes for 2-3× win) had a hidden gotcha. The CDC layer accepts multiple in-flight IRPs (`queueSizeWrite` and `USB_DEVICE_CDC_QUEUE_DEPTH_COMBINED` are both knobs), but the underlying UDPHS device driver only programs the DMA channel in `IRPSubmit`'s queue-empty branch. Subsequent IRPs are linked into the endpoint's queue but *never armed for transmission* — `Tasks_ISR_DMA` advances `irpQueue = irp->next` after a callback fires but doesn't re-program the DMA hardware. Net effect: even with all three layers configured for N=3 in-flight, only one IRP ever transmitted; the other two sat as `STATUS_PENDING` in the linked list forever.

195	**Sink rewrite to N=3 staging ring + counting semaphore.** With multi-IRP working at the driver, [perf_log_sink_cdc.c](../default/src/perf_log/perf_log_sink_cdc.c) swapped the single staging buffer + binary `s_write_done` semaphore for a 3-deep `s_tx_ring[3][SINK_FRAME_BYTES_MAX]` + counting semaphore (init=3) `s_tx_credits`. Producer takes a credit, fills `s_tx_ring[s_tx_head]`, submits non-blocking, advances head; ISR `WRITE_COMPLETE` returns one credit. Single producer (drain task) + FIFO completion order on the bulk endpoint = no race. `SINK_FRAME_BYTES_MAX` derived from `PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES + record/framing overhead, rounded to cache-line` so the two constants can't drift again — the hand-tuned `23104u` literal had already drifted once when the strip max bumped.

State queue was overflowing under STAMP burst traffic — 60 Hz × multiple frame stages plus 240/s FBL_SEND/CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE = ~780/s producer rate. 1024 covers ~1.3 s at full producer rate with drain stalled. Kept after analysis even though current load uses <1% of that — BSS cost is 35 KB on 240 MB cached DDR (rounding error), and the headroom matters if a future strip-size bump pushes toward wire saturation (drain blocks on credit timeouts, state queue accumulates during the block).
198	
199	**Drain-loop fix: drain ALL state records per outer iteration.** First symptom after the multi-IRP work landed: at 185×32 + 290×20 strips (2.14 MB/s), state queue was clean. Bumped strike to 290×32 (2.65 MB/s) and state queue started dropping at 240/s while sink and strip queues stayed clean. Root cause: drain-task loop had `if (xQueueReceive(state_q,…)) WriteFramed(…)` — *one* state record per outer iteration. Strips dominate per-iteration time (~5 ms each on the wire), so state drained at ~50 records/s while produced at ~700/s. Fixed by adding an inner `while` loop that drains every currently-queued state record before moving to the strip drain. After: state delta = 0 across 20 s captures.

200	
201	**Pointer-pool refactor for the strip queue.** FreeRTOS queues are pass-by-value: every `xQueueSend`/`xQueueReceive` does `memcpy(slot, src, item_size)` inside a critical section. With `sizeof(perf_rec_strip_t)` at 23-61 KB depending on `PERF_STRIP_MAX_H`, that's 38-100 µs of *interrupts-off* time per queue op × 240 ops/s = 9-24 ms/s of ISR-latency stretching. Discovered when bumping `PERF_STRIP_MAX_H` to 64 caused the firmware to exhibit erratic behaviour even before any cv_marvin dimension change — the bigger queue items alone were the trigger, via critical-section duration.
202	
203	Refactored: [perf_log.c](../default/src/perf_log/perf_log.c) `s_strip_q` now carries 1-byte slot indices into a static `s_strip_pool[6]` (queue depth + 2 to cover "1 slot in producer's hand, 1 in drain's hand" while preserving drop-on-full semantics). A second small queue, `s_strip_free_q` (depth 6, 1-byte items), holds the free-list. Producer claims a free index, fills the pool slot directly via pointer, queues just the index. Drain dequeues the index, processes via pointer, returns the index to the free list. Removed the producer's `static perf_rec_strip_t r;` and the drain's `static perf_rec_strip_t s_strip_drain;` — same total BSS, no extra copies. Critical sections drop from ~38-100 µs to ~1 µs per queue op.
204	
205	**Fletcher-16 replaces CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE in the framing layer.** Soft CRC bit-by-bit was burning ~26% CPU at 2.65 MB/s — the biggest remaining CPU sink and the cause of the UI sluggishness symptom under load. SAM9X75 has **no CRCCU peripheral** (the journal lever-2 entry was wrong about that — verified by the device pack header list at `packs/SAM9X75D2G_DFP/component/`: AES, SHA, TDES, TRNG, PMECC, but no CRCCU). Hardware-DMA CRC isn't an option on this part.
206	
207	Considered alternatives:
208	
209	| Option | Cycles/byte | CPU @ 2.65 MB/s | Detection |
210	|---|---|---|---|
211	| CRC-16 bit-by-bit (current) | ~25 | ~26% | full CRC strength |
212	| CRC-16 table-driven (256 × u16 LUT) | ~6 | ~6% | full CRC strength |
213	| **Fletcher-16** | **~2** | **~2%** | single-byte changes, adjacent swaps, most non-adjacent swaps; ~1/65536 false-positive rate against random byte sequences |
214	| Sum-16 / XOR-16 | ~1 | ~1% | far weaker (misses swaps and most reorders) |
215	| No checksum | 0 | 0% | rely on USB hardware + record magic + length bounds |
216	
217	USB hardware already CRCs every bulk packet on the wire, so our framing-layer checksum's job is *firmware-side framing-bug detection* + *resync alignment* (false SOF in the middle of a corrupt stream). Both jobs are well-served by Fletcher-16. Picked it.

257	### 2026-05-22 — marvin-perf web viewer: live-mode recording (Phase 3 of 3)
258	
259	Closes the iteration loop. While a live session is up, the user picks an out-dir, hits Record, and the reader thread mirrors validated framed bytes (`FrameBytes.framed`) to `<dir>/perf.bin` directly — no second decode, no resync garbage. Stop / Live-Stop / serial-error all funnel through the same `record_stop()` finalize path that `cli.cmd_record` uses (`finalize_capture_dir(..., source=CaptureSource(kind="serial", port=…))`), so the resulting capture opens cleanly in Offline mode without any extra handling.
260	
261	**Reader-thread tap.** Per-frame, under the session lock: if `_rec` is set, `rec.fh.write(frame.framed)` then bump byte/frame counters. Lock is held briefly (microseconds) — reader is single-producer, control endpoints are the only other contender. Write failures (disk full, ENOSPC) disable the recording in place and post a `record-write` error over the WS rather than tearing down the whole session.
262	
263	**Auto-finalize.** `_LiveSession.stop()` calls `record_stop()` first, while the reader is still alive, so in-flight frames land in the bin instead of being lost to the close race. The reader's own `finally` block also calls `record_stop()` to cover the serial-disconnect path. Both calls hit the same idempotent path (lock-take fh, null `_rec`, close, `finalize_capture_dir`).
264	
265	**REST + WS shape.** `POST /api/live/record/{start,stop}`. Start body `{out_dir}`; 409 on already-recording or session-inactive, 409 on `init_capture_dir(exist_ok=False)` collision so the user gets explicit feedback rather than silently overwriting. Stop is idempotent; returns `{capture_dir, bytes_written, n_frames, manifest}` for scripting use. WS broadcasts `{type:"recording", state:"started"|"stopped", …}` so a passively-attached browser sees state changes from any source — including auto-finalize.
266	
267	**Frontend.** New record-controls toolbar group: out-dir input (suggested `captures/web-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS` on live-start), Record/Stop buttons, and a pill that pulses red while recording. UI flips on the WS broadcast, not the REST response, so a re-attached browser mid-recording reflects reality. Reload during a live recording: `probeLiveSession()` reads `/api/live/status`, sees `recording != null`, re-attaches the WS, and the pill picks up the in-flight session.

269	**Out of scope.** Resumable / appendable recordings (each Record click is a fresh dir), client-side progress meter (REST manifest summary in the stop banner is enough), and dual-mode "open the just-finalized capture in offline tab" auto-handoff.

315	### 2026-05-22 — USB CDC bandwidth headroom + state-queue starvation diagnosis
316	
317	End-to-end strip viewer is up and rendering after the user adjusted strip dimensions in [`cv_marvin_v1.c:341-347`](../default/src/detector/cv_marvin_v1.c#L341-L347) to sensing 185×16 @ (265, 310) and strike 290×20 @ (212, 395). At those dimensions current device→host load is **1.88 MB/s** (≈8.9 KB sensing + ≈17.4 KB strike per frame × 60 Hz + ~25 KB/s state pipeline + ~80 B/frame record overhead) — the link badge is green and `dropped_strip`/`dropped_sink` are flat. But we were dropping at slightly higher dimensions just before this, so our practical CDC-ACM ceiling is < 5 MB/s on this firmware build today. Two concrete things came out of investigating that:
318	
319	**(1) Where the bandwidth is actually going.** The USB-HS bulk-IN theoretical ceiling on UDPHS is ~40-45 MB/s real-world; we're leaving ~85 % of it on the floor. The conservative 5 MB/s working number isn't a USB-HS limit — it's a software-pipeline limit specific to how the sink writes today. Five candidate levers, ranked by expected payoff:
320	
321	  1. **Pipeline writes** ([`perf_log_sink_cdc.c:251-267`](../default/src/perf_log/perf_log_sink_cdc.c#L251-L267)) — biggest single win, expect 2-3×. Today the sink owns a single staging buffer and pends a `WRITE_COMPLETE` semaphore between writes, so the USB DMA sits idle for the round-trip. The CDC write-queue depth is already 3 (`USB_DEVICE_CDC_QUEUE_DEPTH_COMBINED = 3U` in [`configuration.h:243`](../default/src/config/default/configuration.h#L243)) so multi-buffer queueing is supported by the layers below — the sink just doesn't use it. Move to a 2- or 3-deep ring of staging buffers; submit the next write as soon as the previous returns to the queue, not when it completes.
322	  2. **Hardware CRC via CRCCU** — soft CRC at [`perf_log_sink_cdc.c:58-70`](../default/src/perf_log/perf_log_sink_cdc.c#L58-L70) burns ~14 % of CPU at the current rate (byte-at-a-time over every framed payload). CRCCU peripheral does CCITT-FALSE in DMA. Frees CPU for whatever the next bottleneck turns out to be; not a bandwidth knob in itself, but it's the cheapest path to free headroom.
323	  3. **Combine sensing+strike into one wire frame** — saves ~80 B framing overhead per ISC frame (×60 Hz = 4.8 KB/s, ~5-15 % of state-pipeline payload). Small but free if the schema accommodates it; revisit only if (1) and (2) aren't enough.
324	  4. **Move bulk-IN from EP3 → EP2** — UDPHS only exposes 3-bank FIFO depth on EP1-2 ([`drv_usb_udphs_local.h:159`](../default/src/config/default/driver/usb/udphs/src/drv_usb_udphs_local.h#L159) `DRV_USB_UDPHS_EPT_BK = 0x00060000`); EP3-7 are 2-bank only. The current bulk-IN is on EP3 ([`usb_device_init_data.c:213-220`](../default/src/config/default/usb_device_init_data.c#L213-L220)). 3-bank lets the controller pre-load three packets ahead of the host IN tokens; smooths out scheduler micro-stalls. Marginal win unless we're already pipelining at the software layer (so do this *after* lever 1).
325	  5. **Eliminate one memcpy** (architectural) — strip producer copies pixel rows out of the ISC frame into a queue slot, drain task copies that slot bytes onto the wire. Could be reduced to one copy if the strip producer wrote into a sink-owned ring directly, at the cost of tighter coupling between perf_log and the sink. Defer; the ratio of CPU spent in memcpy vs CRC favors lever 2 first.
326	
327	  **What's *not* the bottleneck:** the `DRV_USB_UDPHS_DMA_MAX_TRANSFER_SIZE = 2` knob in [`configuration.h:255`](../default/src/config/default/configuration.h#L255) (multiples of 64 KB, so 128 KB cap). Our largest single record is the 23 KB strip — 5× under the cap. Bumping this to 4 or 8 changes nothing about today's behavior. Documented here because it was the first knob the user noticed and it's tempting to try; save the time.
328	
329	**(2) HWM + RUNTIME records are absent from captures because the state queue is full.** Decoded a 24 s capture — zero `PERF_REC_TASK_HIGHWATER` and zero `PERF_REC_TASK_RUNTIME` records, but `dropped_state since_session = 17188` (~707 dropped/s). Producers are wired and the drain task is calling them every second; the records hit a full queue and get counted as drops instead. Root cause: all state-pipeline records share `s_state_q` ([`perf_log.c:50-52`](../default/src/perf_log/perf_log.c#L50-L52), `PL_STATE_QUEUE_DEPTH = 128`). The 60 Hz × multiple-stage STAMP traffic — especially fretboard_link's `CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE` and `FBL_SEND` pair, which fire on every actuator wire byte — bursts faster than the drain can pull, the queue stays near full, and the once-per-second HWM/RUNTIME emits land on a full queue. Three candidate fixes:
330	
331	  1. **Bump `PL_STATE_QUEUE_DEPTH` from 128 to 1024.** Cheapest. 128 × 32 B/slot = 4 KB today → 32 KB after; static BSS, no malloc. Probably enough on its own — the drain isn't *behind*, it's just unable to absorb burst peaks at 128 slots. Try first.
332	  2. **Give HWM/RUNTIME a dedicated low-pressure queue** drained on the same 1 Hz tick as DROP. Decouples the slow analytics path from the fast stamp path entirely; HWM/RUNTIME can never lose to a stamp burst. More plumbing (second queue + second drain branch) but it's the right shape long-term — and natural alongside lever 1 above (pipelining the sink) since the drain task changes anyway.
333	  3. **Throttle the high-rate stamp producers** — e.g. drop `CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE` to 1-in-N, or roll FBL_SEND/CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE into a single record. Loses information from the timeline; do this only if (1) and (2) both fail.
334	
335	  Going to start with (1) since it's a single `#define` change and HWM is the most useful "is something about to overflow its stack" signal — we want it back before any of the bandwidth-lever work begins, since stack pressure is exactly the kind of thing that surfaces while we're refactoring the sink.
336	
337	Neither finding is being acted on in this session — captured here so the analysis survives context.
338	
339	### 2026-05-22 — Phase 2 perf-log: schema v2 (STRIP + TASK_RUNTIME) wired
340	
341	Schema bump landed end-to-end. Firmware emits the two new record types; host decoder, analyzer, and viewer read them.
342	
343	**Schema v2.** [`perf_log_records.h`](../default/src/perf_log/perf_log_records.h) bumps `PERF_LOG_SCHEMA_VERSION` to 2. `PERF_REC_PATCH (0x05)` is replaced by `PERF_REC_STRIP (0x05)` — variable-length BGR888 region tagged by `perf_strip_kind_t` (SENSING=0, STRIP=1; 256 codes available). `PERF_REC_TASK_RUNTIME (0x08)` adds per-task state/priority/`ulRunTimeCounter` snapshots. Both mirrored on the host in [`records.py`](../../../tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/records.py); `EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION = 2`.
344	
345	**STRIP producer in [`cv_marvin_v1.c`](../default/src/detector/cv_marvin_v1.c).** Two strips per ISC frame, emitted between `detect_frame` and `draw_overlay` so the captured pixels are clean detector input. Sensing line at (240, 295) 240×32, strike line at (240, 400) 240×32 — same coordinates `cv_marvin_v1` already samples for fret detection. Cost: 240×32×3 × 2 × 60 Hz ≈ 2.76 MB/s, well under the 5 MB/s CDC ceiling. The strip queue holds max-sized slots (`PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES = 23040`); drain task computes the on-wire length per record from `(w, h)` so future kinds at smaller dimensions cost only what they emit.
346	
347	**TASK_RUNTIME producer in `perf_log.c`.** 1 Hz alongside the existing HWM emitter — `sample_and_emit_runtimes` fills a static `TaskStatus_t buf[16]` via `uxTaskGetSystemState`, maps each handle to its `perf_task_id_t` via `s_task_handles[]`, and emits `state` (mapped from `eTaskState`), `uxCurrentPriority`, and `ulRunTimeCounter`. Static buffer + bounded loop (no malloc, no recursion). Cost: 24 B × 6 tasks × 1 Hz = 144 B/s.
348	
349	**FreeRTOSConfig.** `INCLUDE_eTaskGetState` flipped 0 → 1 — required for the `eCurrentState` field that `uxTaskGetSystemState` populates. `configRUN_TIME_COUNTER_TYPE = uint64_t` from patch #8 already in place.

31	#define CV_HOLD_RELEASE_FRAC   0.78f
32	#define CV_EDGE_THRESH         25.0f

36	/* Sensor coordinates in native capture-frame space, anchored to 720×480
37	 * (Wii 480p60 — primary production source). (hx,hy) = brightness sensor,
38	 * (ex,ey) = color-filtered edge sensor; both above the strike line.
39	 * Derived from fret-tuner detect_video.py 1920×1080 defaults via the
40	 * same Elgato HDMI capture, scaled by (3/8, 4/9). Runtime calibration
41	 * UI lands with M6. */
42	typedef struct { uint16_t hx, hy, ex, ey; } sensor_xy_t;

53	/* Per-fret BGR target / reject weights. Edge signal is
54	 * (target·c − max(0, reject·c)) × sat_ratio. Reject totals exceed 1.0
55	 * so camera-captured whites with color-temperature bias get suppressed,
56	 * not just mathematically perfect whites. */
57	typedef struct { float target[3]; float reject[3]; } color_filter_t;

59	static const color_filter_t s_color_filter[FRET_COUNT] =

65	    [FRET_ORANGE] = { { 0.0f, 0.3f, 0.7f }, { 1.4f, 0.0f, 0.0f } },
66	};

82	/* ─── Sampling ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
83	
84	/* Average BGR over a (2r+1)×(2r+1) patch centered on (px,py), clipping
85	 * to frame bounds. Center is clamped first so a one-pixel-off calibration
86	 * still produces a reading instead of a silent zero. */
87	static void sample_patch_bgr(const uint8_t *frame, uint16_t fw, uint16_t fh,
88	                             uint16_t px, uint16_t py, float out[3])
89	{
90	    int cx = (int)px;
91	    if (cx < 0)        { cx = 0; }
92	    else if (cx >= fw) { cx = fw - 1; }
93	    int cy = (int)py;
94	    if (cy < 0)        { cy = 0; }
95	    else if (cy >= fh) { cy = fh - 1; }
96	
97	    int r = (int)CV_PATCH_RADIUS;
98	    int x0 = cx - r;       if (x0 < 0)  { x0 = 0; }
99	    int y0 = cy - r;       if (y0 < 0)  { y0 = 0; }
100	    int x1 = cx + r + 1;   if (x1 > fw) { x1 = fw; }
101	    int y1 = cy + r + 1;   if (y1 > fh) { y1 = fh; }
102	
103	    uint32_t sum_b = 0u, sum_g = 0u, sum_r = 0u;
104	    uint32_t row_stride = (uint32_t)fw * CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL;
105	    for (int y = y0; y < y1; y++)
106	    {
107	        const uint8_t *row = frame
108	                           + (uint32_t)y * row_stride
109	                           + (uint32_t)x0 * CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL;
110	        for (int x = x0; x < x1; x++)
111	        {
112	            sum_b += row[0];
113	            sum_g += row[1];
114	            sum_r += row[2];
115	            row   += CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL;
116	        }
117	    }
118	    uint32_t n = (uint32_t)(x1 - x0) * (uint32_t)(y1 - y0);
119	    out[0] = (float)sum_b / (float)n;
120	    out[1] = (float)sum_g / (float)n;
121	    out[2] = (float)sum_r / (float)n;
122	}
123	
124	/* Max channel — triggers on any color or white. */
125	static float brightness(const float bgr[3])
126	{
127	    float m = bgr[0];
128	    if (bgr[1] > m) { m = bgr[1]; }
129	    if (bgr[2] > m) { m = bgr[2]; }
130	    return m;
131	}
132	
133	/* Color-filtered signal scaled by (max-min)/max so white/gray patches
134	 * produce near-zero signal regardless of camera white balance. */
135	static float color_signal(const float bgr[3], const color_filter_t *f)
136	{
137	    float cmax = brightness(bgr);
138	    if (cmax < 1.0f) { return 0.0f; }
139	    float cmin = bgr[0];
140	    if (bgr[1] < cmin) { cmin = bgr[1]; }
141	    if (bgr[2] < cmin) { cmin = bgr[2]; }
142	    float sat = (cmax - cmin) / cmax;
143	
144	    float target = f->target[0]*bgr[0] + f->target[1]*bgr[1] + f->target[2]*bgr[2];
145	    float reject = f->reject[0]*bgr[0] + f->reject[1]*bgr[1] + f->reject[2]*bgr[2];
146	    if (reject < 0.0f) { reject = 0.0f; }
147	    return (target - reject) * sat;
148	}

150	/* ─── Detection ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
151	
152	static void detect_frame(const Video_FrameInfo *frame, QueueHandle_t bus)
153	{
154	    detector_state_t state;
155	    memset(&state, 0, sizeof(state));
156	    state.frame_epoch  = frame->frame_count;
157	    state.timestamp_us = (uint64_t)xTaskGetTickCount() * CV_US_PER_TICK;
158	    state.detector_id  = (uint8_t)DETECTOR_CV_MARVIN_V1;
159	
160	    const float    hold_release = CV_HOLD_THRESH * CV_HOLD_RELEASE_FRAC;
161	    const uint8_t *fbuf = (const uint8_t *)frame->buffer;
162	    uint16_t       fw   = frame->width;
163	    uint16_t       fh   = frame->height;
164	
165	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < FRET_COUNT; i++)
166	    {
167	        sensor_xy_t s = s_sensor_coords[i];
168	        float hold_bgr[3], edge_bgr[3];
169	        sample_patch_bgr(fbuf, fw, fh, s.hx, s.hy, hold_bgr);
170	        sample_patch_bgr(fbuf, fw, fh, s.ex, s.ey, edge_bgr);
171	
172	        float hd = brightness(hold_bgr);
173	        float ed = color_signal(edge_bgr, &s_color_filter[i]);
174	        s_hold_dist[i] = hd;
175	        s_edge_dist[i] = ed;
176	
177	        if (!s_pressed[i] && hd > CV_HOLD_THRESH)   { s_pressed[i] = true;  }
178	        else if (s_pressed[i] && hd < hold_release) { s_pressed[i] = false; }
179	
180	        bool edge_on = ed > CV_EDGE_THRESH;
181	        if (edge_on && !s_edge_active[i]) { s_press_count[i]++; }
182	        s_edge_active[i] = edge_on;
183	
184	        state.fret[i].pressed = s_pressed[i] ? 1u : 0u;
185	
186	        /* confidence: edge_dist scaled to 0..65535. ed lives roughly in
187	         * channel-value units (~0..255) so ×256 fills the range. */
188	        float c = ed * 256.0f;
189	        if (c < 0.0f)        { c = 0.0f;     }
190	        if (c > 65535.0f)    { c = 65535.0f; }
191	        state.fret[i].confidence = (uint16_t)c;
192	
193	        /* raw_value: hold_dist (max channel, 0..255). */
194	        float h = hd;
195	        if (h < 0.0f)        { h = 0.0f;     }
196	        if (h > 65535.0f)    { h = 65535.0f; }
197	        state.fret[i].raw_value = (uint16_t)h;
198	    }
199	
200	    (void)xQueueSend(bus, &state, 0);
201	}

204	
205	/* Paints a per-fret ring at each sample point on the just-sampled frame so
206	 * the user can visually verify alignment with on-screen note targets. The
207	 * ring radius is outside the 5×5 sample patch — overdrawing here would
208	 * not affect *this* frame's reads (detect_frame already ran) but a future
209	 * re-sample on the same ring slot must still see clean source pixels. */
210	#define CV_OVERLAY_RING_R    4u
211	
212	static const uint8_t s_overlay_hold_bgr[3] = { 255u, 255u, 255u };  /* white */
213	static const uint8_t s_overlay_edge_bgr[FRET_COUNT][3] =
214	{   /* { B,    G,    R } */
215	    [FRET_GREEN]  = {   0u, 255u,   0u },
216	    [FRET_RED]    = {   0u,   0u, 255u },
217	    [FRET_YELLOW] = {   0u, 255u, 255u },
218	    [FRET_BLUE]   = { 255u,   0u,   0u },
219	    [FRET_ORANGE] = {   0u, 165u, 255u },

222	static inline void put_pixel_bgr(uint8_t *frame, int fw, int fh,
223	                                 int x, int y,
224	                                 uint8_t b, uint8_t g, uint8_t r)
225	{
226	    if (x < 0 || x >= fw || y < 0 || y >= fh) { return; }
227	    uint8_t *p = frame + ((uint32_t)y * (uint32_t)fw + (uint32_t)x) * CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL;
228	    p[0] = b; p[1] = g; p[2] = r;
229	}
230	
231	/* Bresenham midpoint circle — perimeter only, 8-way symmetric. */
232	static void draw_ring(uint8_t *frame, int fw, int fh,
233	                      int cx, int cy, int radius,
234	                      uint8_t b, uint8_t g, uint8_t r)
235	{
236	    int x = radius, y = 0, err = 0;
237	    while (x >= y)
238	    {
239	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx + x, cy + y, b, g, r);
240	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx + y, cy + x, b, g, r);
241	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx - y, cy + x, b, g, r);
242	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx - x, cy + y, b, g, r);
243	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx - x, cy - y, b, g, r);
244	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx - y, cy - x, b, g, r);
245	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx + y, cy - x, b, g, r);
246	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx + x, cy - y, b, g, r);
247	        y++;
248	        err += 1 + 2 * y;
249	        if (2 * (err - x) + 1 > 0) { x--; err += 1 - 2 * x; }
250	    }
251	}
252	
253	static void draw_filled_disk(uint8_t *frame, int fw, int fh,
254	                             int cx, int cy, int radius,
255	                             uint8_t b, uint8_t g, uint8_t r)
256	{
257	    int rr = radius * radius;
258	    for (int dy = -radius; dy <= radius; dy++)
259	    {
260	        for (int dx = -radius; dx <= radius; dx++)
261	        {
262	            if (dx * dx + dy * dy <= rr)
263	            {
264	                put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx + dx, cy + dy, b, g, r);
265	            }
266	        }
267	    }
268	}
269	
270	/* Per-fret marker: position ring (always) + center dot when the matching
271	 * detector is firing this frame. Hold dot = white => brightness over
272	 * threshold. Edge dot = fret color => color-filtered edge over threshold.
273	 * Lets the user watch chatter live: a stable note should show a steady
274	 * dot for the hold duration; a strum window should flash the edge dot
275	 * once. Constant flicker = noise pushing thresholds. */
276	#define CV_OVERLAY_DOT_R     1u
277	
278	static void draw_overlay(uint8_t *frame, uint16_t fw, uint16_t fh)
279	{
280	    int w = (int)fw, h = (int)fh;
281	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < FRET_COUNT; i++)
282	    {
283	        sensor_xy_t s = s_sensor_coords[i];
284	        const uint8_t *e = s_overlay_edge_bgr[i];
285	
286	        draw_ring(frame, w, h, s.hx, s.hy, (int)CV_OVERLAY_RING_R,
287	                  s_overlay_hold_bgr[0], s_overlay_hold_bgr[1], s_overlay_hold_bgr[2]);
288	        draw_ring(frame, w, h, s.ex, s.ey, (int)CV_OVERLAY_RING_R,
289	                  e[0], e[1], e[2]);
290	
291	        if (s_pressed[i])
292	        {
293	            draw_filled_disk(frame, w, h, s.hx, s.hy, (int)CV_OVERLAY_DOT_R,
294	                             s_overlay_hold_bgr[0], s_overlay_hold_bgr[1], s_overlay_hold_bgr[2]);
295	        }
296	        if (s_edge_active[i])
297	        {
298	            draw_filled_disk(frame, w, h, s.ex, s.ey, (int)CV_OVERLAY_DOT_R,
299	                             e[0], e[1], e[2]);
300	        }
301	    }
302	}

306	static void cv_marvin_v1_task(void *param)
307	{
308	    (void)param;
309	
310	    QueueHandle_t frames = xQueueCreateStatic(CV_FRAME_QUEUE_DEPTH,
311	                                              sizeof(Video_FrameInfo),
312	                                              s_frame_queue_storage,
313	                                              &s_frame_queue_buf);

316	    configASSERT(subscribed);
317	
318	    QueueHandle_t bus = Detector_BusQueue();
319	    configASSERT(bus != NULL);
320	
321	    LOG_INFO("CV: cv_marvin_v1 started\r\n");
322	
323	    for (;;)
324	    {
325	        Video_FrameInfo frame;
326	        if (xQueueReceive(frames, &frame, portMAX_DELAY) != pdTRUE) { continue; }
327	
328	        /* Always drain, even when disabled, so frames don't back up. */
329	        if (!Detector_IsEnabled(DETECTOR_CV_MARVIN_V1)) { continue; }
330	        if (frame.buffer == NULL)                       { continue; }
331	        if (frame.width == 0u || frame.height == 0u)    { continue; }
332	        if (frame.bytes_per_pixel != CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL){ continue; }
333	
334	        PerfLog_EmitStamp(PERF_STAGE_CV_START, frame.frame_count, 0u);
335	        detect_frame(&frame, bus);
336	        PerfLog_EmitStamp(PERF_STAGE_CV_END, frame.frame_count, 0u);
337	
338	        /* Sensing strip centers on the sensor row (y=311); strike strip is
339	         * below the sensors at the strum trigger zone. Both pre-overlay so
340	         * the host viewer sees the same pixels the detector consumed. */
341	        const uint32_t fstride = (uint32_t)frame.width * CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL;
342	        PerfLog_EmitStripFromFrame(frame.frame_count, PERF_STRIP_SENSING,
343	                                   (const uint8_t *)frame.buffer, fstride,
344	                                   265u, 300, 185u, 32u);
345	        PerfLog_EmitStripFromFrame(frame.frame_count, PERF_STRIP_STRIKE,
346	                                   (const uint8_t *)frame.buffer, fstride,
347	                                   212u, 395u, 290u, 32u);
348	
349	        draw_overlay((uint8_t *)frame.buffer, frame.width, frame.height);
350	
351	        // /* ~2 Hz signal dump for threshold tuning. hold/edge values shown
352	        //  * vs the 50 threshold, with P/E flags reflecting current state. */
353	        // if ((frame.frame_count % 30u) == 0u)

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-06-01 15:31:44Z)**_

**Where the spec lives today.** The wire-format source of truth is the inline comments in [`perf_log_records.h`](firmware/marvin/default/src/perf_log/perf_log_records.h) — every record type has a one-paragraph "what this is, what its fields mean" comment, and the host mirror in [`marvin_perf/records.py`](tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/records.py) tracks it. There's no separate prose doc that explains the *purpose* of each type — the comments cover field-level meaning, but nothing groups them into "low-level framing/integrity vs. tuning channels." That's a real gap if we're about to pivot the channel's role.

**Records sorted by what they're for, today:**

| Category | Records | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Integrity / framing | SOF+LEN+Fletcher-16 framer, `SESSION` (schema version + timer_freq_hz), `DROP` (cumulative loss counters) | Low-level — proves bytes survived the wire and the host is reading the same schema. **Keep all.** |
| Pipeline timing | `STAMP` (per-stage timestamps), `TIMING` (chord-window/FIFO/strum_dir snapshot) | Mid-level — answers "where did the frame's latency go" and "what did the timing pipeline emit." |
| Health | `TASK_HIGHWATER`, `TASK_RUNTIME` | Low-rate diagnostic — stack/CPU per task. |
| Algorithm state | `DETECTOR` (5 hold + 5 edge values, pressed_mask, edge_active_mask), `STRIP` (BGR888 ROI) | The only "what is the algorithm thinking" channels we have today. Both are thin. |

**What the pivot needs.** The DETECTOR record gives you per-fret hold/edge *values* but not the *coordinates*, *thresholds*, or *color filter weights* — so the host can plot a number but can't draw it onto the strip in the right place, or draw the threshold line. Three concrete additions would carry it:

1. **A `DETECTOR_CONFIG` record** (low-rate, on change or once per second) — sample coords (`hx,hy,ex,ey` per fret), `hold_thresh`, `release_frac`, `edge_thresh`, color-filter target/reject weights. Static in firmware today, but the host needs them to render overlays correctly and they'll become tunable later.
2. **An `ACTUATOR` record** — richer than the existing `FBL_SEND` stamp: the chord queue's *intended* mask, the *asserted* mask, strum_dir, and the actuator-side ack delta (`assert_at` vs observed via `CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE`). Today this is split across `TIMING` + two stamps; pulling it together makes "what is the actuator doing right now" a single-record question.
3. **Strip annotations** — add a `kind` per fret on the `DETECTOR` record (or a sibling record carrying *just* sample readings tagged to strip-relative coords) so the host can paint sample dots / threshold bars onto the SENSING and STRIKE strips at render time. Keeps the strip producer cheap (raw pixels only); annotations are firmware-side state, host composites them.

**Tradeoff** to call out: each new record type widens the wire and the schema. We're at 2.77 MB/s with headroom, so cost is fine — but every addition is a schema bump on both sides. Worth bundling these so we do one v3 cut, not three.

Want me to draft a doc that walks through each record type's purpose (the gap above), or jump straight to designing the v3 schema additions?

You're right, (3) is redundant. (1) gives sample coordinates in frame space; the strip records already carry their own `(x, y, w, h)` in frame space; subtracting gives strip-relative pixel coordinates trivially. The per-frame readings already live in `DETECTOR` (`hold_dist`, `edge_dist`) at the same rate as `STRIP`, correlated by `frame_epoch`. So everything the overlay needs is on the wire once (1) lands — the rest is host-side rendering.

Net: two new record types — `DETECTOR_CONFIG` (sample coords, thresholds, filter weights, low-rate / on-change) and `ACTUATOR` (intended mask, asserted mask, strum_dir, ack timing) — plus host-side overlay code in marvin-perf that reads existing `STRIP` + `DETECTOR` + new `DETECTOR_CONFIG` and paints sample dots / threshold lines on the strip canvas.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-06-01 15:40:09Z)**_

Mostly yes, with two honest gaps:

**Detector — complete.** Raw pixels (STRIP) + sample coords (new DETECTOR_CONFIG) + intermediate values (DETECTOR's `hold_dist`/`edge_dist`) + thresholds (new DETECTOR_CONFIG) + output (DETECTOR's pressed/edge masks). Host can reproduce every step of `detect_frame` and prove the firmware's decision matches what the pixels actually say.

**Timing pipeline — partial.** TIMING gives `publish_mask`, `chord_window_fill`, `fifo_depth`, `strum_dir` — that's the *output*, not the contents. We can't see *which* per-fret detector states are sitting in the chord window or the delay FIFO. For tuning the chord/strum scheduling specifically, that opacity will bite — "why did it publish *that* mask" isn't answerable from the wire today.

**Actuator — covered by the new ACTUATOR record**, but one thing worth carrying alongside it: the active producer. `fretboard_link` has multiple producers (`timing_pipeline`, `manual_control`, future game-state controller per spec §4.8) with mode-level arbitration one layer up. When manual_control takes the wire, today nothing on the wire indicates the handoff — the published mask just changes source. A 1-byte `producer_id` field in ACTUATOR closes that.

So: full coverage of the detector pivot, plus a small ask to widen TIMING (window/FIFO contents, not just counts) if chord/strum scheduling is also in scope for tuning. If today's pivot is just detector + actuator wire, what's proposed is sufficient.

268	}

294	static void process_frame(const detector_state_t *state)
295	{
296	    /* Detector frame timestamps drive the clock so this is replay-
297	     * deterministic. timestamp_us is monotonic per spec §4.2.3. */
298	    s_now_ms = (uint32_t)(state->timestamp_us / 1000ull);
299	    s_last_frame_us = state->timestamp_us;
300	
301	    uint8_t presses, releases, pressed_mask;
302	    derive_edges(state, &presses, &releases, &pressed_mask);
303	
304	    if (presses)
305	    {
306	        if (!s_chord_open)
307	        {
308	            s_chord_open     = true;
309	            s_chord_start_ms = s_now_ms;
310	            s_chord_mask     = 0u;
311	        }
312	        s_chord_mask |= presses;
313	    }
314	
315	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < FRET_COUNT; i++)
316	    {
317	        if (releases & s_fret_bit[i])
318	        {
319	            s_release_at_ms[i]      = s_now_ms + TP_STRUM_DELAY_MS;
320	            s_release_pending_mask |= s_fret_bit[i];
321	        }
322	    }
323	
324	    advance(pressed_mask);
325	
326	    PerfLog_EmitStamp(PERF_STAGE_TP_TICK, state->frame_epoch,
327	                      (uint32_t)s_output_mask);
328	}

330	static void timing_pipeline_task(void *param)
331	{
332	    (void)param;
333	
334	    QueueHandle_t bus = Detector_BusQueue();
335	    configASSERT(bus != NULL);
336	
337	    LOG_INFO("TIMING: pipeline started\r\n");
338	
339	    for (;;)
340	    {
341	        detector_state_t state;
342	        if (xQueueReceive(bus, &state, pdMS_TO_TICKS(TP_TICK_MS)) == pdTRUE)
343	        {
344	            if ((detector_id_t)state.detector_id != Detector_GetActive())
345	            {
346	                continue;
347	            }
348	            process_frame(&state);
349	        }
350	        else
351	        {
352	            /* No new frame; advance the clock so deadlines that fell
353	             * between frames (strum pulses, release timers) still fire. */
354	            s_now_ms += TP_TICK_MS;
355	            advance(s_prev_pressed_mask);
356	        }
357	    }
358	}

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-06-01 15:46:54Z)**_

Read through [`timing_pipeline.c`](firmware/marvin/default/src/actuator/timing_pipeline.c). Hidden state today:

- **Chord window**: `s_chord_open`, `s_chord_start_ms`, `s_chord_mask` — accumulating mask while the 30 ms window is open.
- **Note queue** (32-deep): each entry is `{assert_at_ms, fret_mask}` — when each pending chord will land on the wire.
- **Strum queue** (32-deep): each entry is `{strum_at_ms, fret_mask}` — scheduled strum pulses.
- **Active state**: `s_frets_active` (asserted mask, pre-strum), `s_strum_active` + `s_strum_release_at_ms`, `s_strum_direction` (next dir).
- **Release timers**: `s_release_pending_mask` + per-fret `s_release_at_ms[]` — held-note release suppression.

Current TIMING record gives counts (`chord_window_fill`, `fifo_depth`) but no masks, no deadlines, no chord-window mask. So the host sees "3 things queued" without knowing what they are or when they fire.

**Proposal — extend TIMING into a per-frame snapshot:**

| Field | Bytes | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `now_ms` | 4 | Pipeline's clock — anchors all `*_at_ms` deltas |
| `chord_open`, `chord_age_ms`, `chord_mask` | 1+2+1 | What's accumulating in the window right now |
| `note_q_count`, `note_head_at_ms`, `note_head_mask`, `note_tail_mask` | 1+4+1+1 | Front-of-queue (next to fire) + union of remaining |
| `strum_q_count`, `strum_head_at_ms`, `strum_head_mask`, `strum_dir_next` | 1+4+1+1 | Same shape for the strum queue |
| `frets_active`, `strum_active`, `strum_release_at_ms` | 1+1+4 | What's currently asserted, strum still in pulse |
| `release_pending_mask`, `release_min_at_ms` | 1+4 | Earliest pending release deadline |
| `publish_mask` (kept) | 1 | Final wire output |

Roughly 36 B body, fits well under the existing wire budget — once per detector frame (60 Hz) is ~2 KB/s.

**What this buys.** Host can answer "why did it publish that mask at frame N" by replaying detector events forward through the visible queue state. Doesn't capture full causal trace (every push/pop) but covers "what's the pipeline thinking right now," which is what tuning needs. If we ever need causal trace, a sibling `TIMING_EVENT` record on push/pop is a clean follow-up.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-06-01 15:53:21Z)**_

**What we already have via TASK_RUNTIME**: per-task `ulRunTimeCounter` (driven by 64-bit SYS_TIME counter, patch #8). The journal's CPU% table is computed as Δrun_time / Σ Δrun_time across *recorded* tasks — that's why it says "idle excluded" and "single-digit % absolute" is an inference, not a measurement.

**One small gap, easy fix.** Idle task isn't registered. Add:

```c
PerfLog_RegisterTaskForHighwater(PERF_TASK_IDLE, xTaskGetIdleTaskHandle());
```

at perf_log init. Then the host computes absolute CPU% = `1 − idle_delta / Σ_all_delta`. Single line plus an enum entry.

**Second small gap.** MCC-owned tasks (XLCDC, MAXTOUCH, LEGATO, SYS_INPUT, USB host driver tasks) aren't in `s_task_handles[]`, so their CPU is invisible. Two options:
- **Cheap**: add an `OTHER` pseudo-slot that emits `(Σ all-task runtime) − (Σ registered-task runtime) − idle` once per second. Closes the books — every cycle accounted to marvin task / idle / other.
- **Richer**: expose all tasks `uxTaskGetSystemState` returns by name. Bigger schema change (strings or a much longer enum). Skip unless we actually need to break out individual MCC tasks.

**Other FreeRTOS / system metrics I'd skip:**
- **Free heap.** Heap_1 only — never frees, so post-init it's static. No dynamic signal.
- **Legato internal heap.** Separate pool, no clean introspection API. Carried as an open question already.
- **Cortex-A5 PMU** (cache misses, cycles, instructions). Real instrumentation cost, value uncertain. Defer until a perf hunt actually needs it.
- **ISR latency / context-switch count.** Already implicit — STAMP records with `FROM_ISR` flag carry ISR entry timestamps; ts_counter deltas across stages give task-handoff latency.

So: idle + OTHER pseudo-slot bundled into the v3 schema bump alongside DETECTOR_CONFIG / ACTUATOR / extended TIMING. That gives complete CPU accounting plus full visibility into detection + actuator decisions.

Want me to write this up as a journal entry to lock in the v3 plan before we start cutting code?

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-06-01 16:06:18Z)**_

Yes — the wire format already supports per-window math. TASK_RUNTIME emits `run_time_counter` (cumulative since boot) at 1 Hz; host subtracts adjacent records to get the per-second delta. The journal's "CV_MARVIN 71.97% / PERF_DRAIN 26.99% / …" table was computed exactly that way.

Wrap is fine: the wire field is `uint32_t` (low 32 of FreeRTOS's now-64-bit counter per patch #8). At 266 MHz, a 1-second window delta is ~266M counts — well under 2³² with modular subtraction handling any cumulative wrap.

**Status check on the viewer side:** [`web/api.py:362-402`](tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/web/api.py#L362-L402) — the `/capture/{id}/rtos` endpoint still returns `"cpu_pct": None  # Phase 2` and `"cpu_pct_idle": None  # Phase 2`. So the data is on the wire, the math is straightforward, but the host viewer hasn't shipped the per-window CPU% display yet. That's a marvin-perf code task that bundles cleanly with the v3 work — once IDLE + OTHER are wired on the firmware side, the viewer endpoint fills in those `None` slots with `Δrun_time / Σ Δrun_time` per window.

So bundling this all into v3:

1. **Wire format**: `DETECTOR_CONFIG` (new), `ACTUATOR` (new, with `producer_id`), extended `TIMING` (~36 B body), add `PERF_TASK_IDLE` + `PERF_TASK_OTHER` enum slots.
2. **Firmware**: register idle handle; emit OTHER as `Σ all − Σ registered − idle` from `uxTaskGetSystemState` once per second; producers for the new records.
3. **Host**: schema mirror, RTOS endpoint computes per-window CPU%, viewer overlays sample dots / threshold lines on STRIP using DETECTOR_CONFIG + DETECTOR.

208	        {

210	            PerfLog_EmitTaskRuntime((perf_task_id_t)i,
211	                                    map_task_state(t->eCurrentState),
212	                                    (uint8_t)t->uxCurrentPriority,
213	                                    (uint32_t)t->ulRunTimeCounter);
214	            break;
215	        }
216	    }
217	}
218	
219	static void perf_log_drain_task(void *param)
220	{
221	    (void)param;
222	
223	    PerfLogSinkCdc_Initialize();
224	    s_running = true;
225	
226	    TickType_t last_drop = xTaskGetTickCount();
227	    bool prev_connected = false;
228	
229	    for (;;)
230	    {
231	        bool now_connected = PerfLogSinkCdc_IsConnected();
232	        if (now_connected && !prev_connected)
233	        {
234	            emit_session_record();
235	        }
236	        prev_connected = now_connected;
237	
238	        perf_rec_state_slot_t srec;
239	        if (xQueueReceive(s_state_q, &srec,
240	                          pdMS_TO_TICKS(PL_DRAIN_RX_TIMEOUT_MS)) == pdTRUE)
241	        {
242	            PerfLogSinkCdc_WriteFramed(&srec, record_size(&srec));
243	            /* Drain all currently queued state records before moving on.
244	             * Strips cost ~5 ms apiece on the wire, so a one-state-per-
245	             * iteration loop runs at ~50 Hz under load — well below the
246	             * ~700 stamps/s production rate. Same shape as the strip
247	             * drain below. */
248	            while (xQueueReceive(s_state_q, &srec, 0) == pdTRUE)
249	            {
250	                PerfLogSinkCdc_WriteFramed(&srec, record_size(&srec));
251	            }
252	        }
253	
254	        /* Strip drain: dequeue slot index, write the slot's data via
255	         * pointer (no copy), return slot to the free pool. */
256	        uint8_t slot_idx;
257	        while (xQueueReceive(s_strip_q, &slot_idx, 0) == pdTRUE)
258	        {
259	            const perf_rec_strip_t *r = &s_strip_pool[slot_idx];
260	            PerfLogSinkCdc_WriteFramed(r, strip_record_size(r));
261	            (void)xQueueSend(s_strip_free_q, &slot_idx, 0);
262	        }
263	
264	        if ((xTaskGetTickCount() - last_drop) >= pdMS_TO_TICKS(PL_DROP_REPORT_PERIOD_MS))
265	        {
266	            last_drop = xTaskGetTickCount();
267	            emit_drop_record();
268	            sample_and_emit_hwms();
269	            sample_and_emit_runtimes();
270	        }
271	    }
272	}

279	                                   sizeof(perf_rec_state_slot_t),

291	                                        sizeof(uint8_t),
292	                                        s_strip_free_q_storage,
293	                                        &s_strip_free_q_buf);
294	    configASSERT(s_strip_free_q != NULL);
295	
296	    /* Seed the free list with all pool indices. */
297	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < PL_STRIP_POOL_SIZE; i++)
298	    {
299	        (void)xQueueSend(s_strip_free_q, &i, 0);
300	    }
301	}

328	/* Drop counters are RMW from both task (send_state, EmitPatch,
329	 * NoteSinkDrop) and ISR (EmitStampFromISR) contexts. ARM926 single-
330	 * issue makes a single 32-bit aligned store atomic, but the increment
331	 * is LDR/ADD/STR — an ISR firing between LDR and STR loses an increment.
332	 * Critical sections (which globally disable IRQs on this port) keep
333	 * the RMW indivisible. The counters are diagnostic, so the very brief
334	 * IRQ-off window is fine. */
335	static inline void counter_add_task(volatile uint32_t *p, uint32_t v)
336	{
337	    taskENTER_CRITICAL();
338	    *p += v;
339	    taskEXIT_CRITICAL();
340	}
341	
342	static inline void counter_add_isr(volatile uint32_t *p, uint32_t v)
343	{
344	    UBaseType_t s = taskENTER_CRITICAL_FROM_ISR();
345	    *p += v;
346	    taskEXIT_CRITICAL_FROM_ISR(s);
347	}
348	
349	static inline void send_state(const perf_rec_state_slot_t *slot)
350	{
351	    if (s_state_q == NULL) { return; }
352	    if (!type_enabled(slot->hdr.type)) { return; }
353	    if (xQueueSend(s_state_q, slot, 0) != pdTRUE)
354	    {
355	        counter_add_task(&s_drop_state, 1u);
356	    }
357	}

365	    slot.stamp.aux      = aux;

426	/* Strip producer: claim a free slot from the pool, row-copy a w×h BGR888
427	 * region out of the strided source frame directly into the slot, then
428	 * enqueue just the slot index. No struct memcpy in the queue critical
429	 * section — only a 1-byte index transfer.
430	 *
431	 * Total pixel bytes (w*h*3) must fit the slot's bgr[] capacity
432	 * (PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES); per-axis shape is unconstrained beyond that.
433	 * Drop-on-pool-empty; counter incremented under critical section. */
434	void PerfLog_EmitStripFromFrame(uint32_t frame_epoch,
435	                                perf_strip_kind_t kind,
436	                                const uint8_t *frame, uint32_t frame_stride,
437	                                uint16_t x, uint16_t y,
438	                                uint16_t w, uint16_t h)
439	{
440	    if (s_strip_q == NULL || s_strip_free_q == NULL || frame == NULL) { return; }
441	    if (!type_enabled(PERF_REC_STRIP)) { return; }
442	    if (w == 0u || h == 0u) { return; }
443	    if ((uint32_t)w * (uint32_t)h * PERF_STRIP_BPP > PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES) { return; }
444	
445	    uint8_t slot_idx;
446	    if (xQueueReceive(s_strip_free_q, &slot_idx, 0) != pdTRUE)
447	    {
448	        counter_add_task(&s_drop_strip, 1u);
449	        return;
450	    }
451	
452	    perf_rec_strip_t *r = &s_strip_pool[slot_idx];
453	    memset(r, 0, PERF_STRIP_HDR_BYTES);
454	    hdr_fill(&r->hdr, PERF_REC_STRIP, 0u, frame_epoch);
455	    r->x    = x;
456	    r->y    = y;
457	    r->w    = w;
458	    r->h    = h;
459	    r->kind = (uint8_t)kind;
460	
461	    const uint32_t row_bytes = (uint32_t)w * PERF_STRIP_BPP;
462	    const uint8_t *src = frame + (uint32_t)y * frame_stride + (uint32_t)x * PERF_STRIP_BPP;
463	    uint8_t *dst = r->bgr;
464	    for (uint16_t row = 0u; row < h; row++)
465	    {
466	        memcpy(dst, src, row_bytes);
467	        src += frame_stride;
468	        dst += row_bytes;
469	    }
470	
471	    if (xQueueSend(s_strip_q, &slot_idx, 0) != pdTRUE)
472	    {
473	        /* In-flight queue full (pool sized depth+2 makes this rare; only
474	         * possible if the drain task is blocked while strip_q is at depth
475	         * and the producer also holds a slot). Return slot to free pool. */
476	        (void)xQueueSend(s_strip_free_q, &slot_idx, 0);
477	        counter_add_task(&s_drop_strip, 1u);
478	    }
479	}
480	
481	/* ─── Emit (ISR context) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
482	
483	void PerfLog_EmitStampFromISR(perf_stage_t stage,
484	                              uint32_t frame_epoch,
485	                              uint32_t aux,
486	                              BaseType_t *higher_priority_task_woken)
487	{
488	    if (s_state_q == NULL) { return; }
489	    if (!type_enabled(PERF_REC_STAMP)) { return; }
490	    perf_rec_state_slot_t slot;
491	    memset(&slot, 0, sizeof(slot));
492	    hdr_fill(&slot.stamp.hdr, PERF_REC_STAMP, PERF_FLAG_FROM_ISR, frame_epoch);
493	    slot.stamp.stage_id = (uint8_t)stage;
494	    slot.stamp.aux      = aux;
495	    if (xQueueSendFromISR(s_state_q, &slot, higher_priority_task_woken) != pdTRUE)
496	    {
497	        counter_add_isr(&s_drop_state, 1u);
498	    }
499	}

12	/* Per-frame performance log. Producers post records onto two static
13	 * queues (small / patch); a low-priority drain task frames them
14	 * (SOF + length + payload + CRC-16/CCITT) and pushes the bytes out the
15	 * USB-device CDC sink. Drop-on-full, never block. The pipeline must
16	 * remain unaffected if perf-log vanishes.
17	 *
18	 * All emit calls take ≈O(memcpy) and never lock. The ISR variants use
19	 * xQueueSendFromISR; the task variants use xQueueSend with zero block
20	 * time. Choose by call site — passing the wrong one will not corrupt
21	 * state but may misuse the higher_priority_task_woken pathway. */
22

24	void PerfLog_Start(void);          /* call after vTaskStartScheduler */

61	static USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT_RESPONSE cdc_event_handler(USB_HOST_CDC_HANDLE handle,
62	                                                    USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT event,

64	                                                    uintptr_t context)

79	            portYIELD_FROM_ISR(hpw);

83	        case USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT_ACM_SET_CONTROL_LINE_STATE_COMPLETE:
84	        {

87	            portYIELD_FROM_ISR(hpw);

137	    {
138	        .dwDTERate   = FBL_BAUDRATE,
139	        .bCharFormat = USB_CDC_LINE_CODING_STOP_1_BIT,
140	        .bParityType = USB_CDC_LINE_CODING_PARITY_NONE,
141	        .bDataBits   = USB_CDC_LINE_CODING_DATA_8_BIT,
142	    };
143	    USB_HOST_CDC_REQUEST_HANDLE rh;
144	    (void)xSemaphoreTake(s_ctrl_done, 0);
145	    if (USB_HOST_CDC_ACM_LineCodingSet(h, &rh, &line_coding) == USB_HOST_CDC_RESULT_SUCCESS)
146	    {
147	        (void)xSemaphoreTake(s_ctrl_done, pdMS_TO_TICKS(FBL_CTRL_TIMEOUT_MS));
148	    }
149	
150	    /* Some EDBG-CDC firmwares hold the bridge UART idle until the host
151	     * raises DTR. Assert DTR + carrier so the bridge actually drives
152	     * bytes out to the fretboard MCU's SERCOM1 RX. */
153	    static USB_CDC_CONTROL_LINE_STATE cls = { .dtr = 1u, .carrier = 1u };
154	    (void)xSemaphoreTake(s_ctrl_done, 0);
155	    if (USB_HOST_CDC_ACM_ControlLineStateSet(h, &rh, &cls) == USB_HOST_CDC_RESULT_SUCCESS)
156	    {
157	        (void)xSemaphoreTake(s_ctrl_done, pdMS_TO_TICKS(FBL_CTRL_TIMEOUT_MS));
158	    }
159	
160	    s_cdc_handle = h;
161	    s_connected  = true;
162	    LOG_INFO("FBL: CDC device attached, handle opened\r\n");
163	    return true;
164	}
165	
166	static bool send_one_byte(uint8_t mask)
167	{
168	    if (!s_connected) { return false; }
169	
170	    static uint8_t tx_byte;
171	    tx_byte = (uint8_t)(mask & 0x7F);
172	
173	    /* Drain any prior signal so we wait for *this* write's completion. */
174	    (void)xSemaphoreTake(s_write_done, 0);
175	
176	    USB_HOST_CDC_TRANSFER_HANDLE th;
177	    USB_HOST_CDC_RESULT r = USB_HOST_CDC_Write(s_cdc_handle, &th, &tx_byte, 1u);
178	    if (r != USB_HOST_CDC_RESULT_SUCCESS)
179	    {
180	        LOG_WARN("FBL: CDC_Write rejected, r=%d\r\n", (int)r);
181	        return false;
182	    }
183	    PerfLog_EmitStamp(PERF_STAGE_FBL_SEND, 0u, (uint32_t)tx_byte);
184	
185	    if (xSemaphoreTake(s_write_done, pdMS_TO_TICKS(FBL_WRITE_TIMEOUT_MS)) != pdTRUE)
186	    {
187	        LOG_WARN("FBL: write timeout, marking detached\r\n");
188	        close_cdc();
189	        return false;
190	    }
191	    if (s_last_write_result != USB_HOST_CDC_RESULT_SUCCESS)
192	    {
193	        LOG_WARN("FBL: write completion err=%d\r\n", (int)s_last_write_result);
194	        return false;
195	    }
196	    return true;
197	}
198	
199	static void fretboard_link_task(void *param)
200	{
201	    (void)param;
202	
203	    LOG_INFO("FBL: fretboard link started\r\n");
204	
205	    uint8_t last_mask = 0u;
206	
207	    for (;;)
208	    {
209	        if (s_cdc_obj_valid && s_cdc_handle == USB_HOST_CDC_HANDLE_INVALID)
210	        {
211	            s_cdc_obj_valid = false;
212	            (void)open_cdc(s_cdc_obj_pending);
213	        }
214	
215	        uint8_t mask;
216	        if (xQueueReceive(s_cmd_queue, &mask, pdMS_TO_TICKS(FBL_HEARTBEAT_MS)) == pdTRUE)
217	        {
218	            last_mask = mask;
219	        }
220	        else
221	        {
222	            mask = last_mask;
223	        }
224	
225	        if (s_connected)
226	        {
227	            (void)send_one_byte(mask);
228	        }
229	    }
230	}
231	
232	void FretboardLink_Initialize(void)
233	{
234	    s_cmd_queue = xQueueCreateStatic(FBL_CMD_QUEUE_DEPTH,
235	                                     sizeof(uint8_t),
236	                                     s_cmd_queue_storage,
237	                                     &s_cmd_queue_buf);
238	    configASSERT(s_cmd_queue != NULL);
239	
240	    s_write_done = xSemaphoreCreateBinaryStatic(&s_write_done_buf);
241	    configASSERT(s_write_done != NULL);
242	
243	    s_ctrl_done = xSemaphoreCreateBinaryStatic(&s_ctrl_done_buf);
244	    configASSERT(s_ctrl_done != NULL);
245	
246	    /* Register the CDC attach listener before the bus is enabled — the host
247	     * stack only matches a class driver if its attach handler is in place
248	     * when enumeration completes. App-level USB_HOST_BusEnable runs right
249	     * after this init returns. */
250	    (void)USB_HOST_CDC_AttachEventHandlerSet(cdc_attach_handler, 0u);
251	
252	    TaskHandle_t h = xTaskCreateStatic(fretboard_link_task,
253	                                       "FretLink",
254	                                       FBL_TASK_STACK_WORDS,
255	                                       NULL,
256	                                       FBL_TASK_PRIORITY,
257	                                       s_task_stack,
258	                                       &s_task_tcb);
259	    PerfLog_RegisterTaskForHighwater(PERF_TASK_FRETBOARD_LINK, h);
260	}
261	
262	bool FretboardLink_IsConnected(void)
263	{
264	    return s_connected;
265	}
266	
267	void FretboardLink_Send(uint8_t mask)
268	{
269	    if (s_cmd_queue == NULL) { return; }
270	    uint8_t v = (uint8_t)(mask & 0x7F);
271	    /* Overwrite is strictly latest-wins: a newer producer's mask replaces
272	     * any unsent older one — keeps a stalled USB write from accumulating
273	     * stale chord state. */
274	    (void)xQueueOverwrite(s_cmd_queue, &v);
275	}

7	/* Fretboard link — USB CDC host writer that ferries a 7-bit GPIO bitmask
8	 * to the fretboard MCU as a stream of single-byte messages. Spec §4.4
9	 * actuator transport. Initialize first among the actuator modules so the
10	 * submit queue exists by the time any producer task starts running. Also
11	 * enables the USB host bus, so call after SYS_Initialize.
12	 *
13	 * Producers — timing_pipeline today, game menu controller (spec §4.8) and
14	 * manual test inputs in the future — all submit through FretboardLink_Send.
15	 * Latest-wins semantics: a newer mask overwrites an unsent older one, so
16	 * a stalled USB write can't accumulate stale state. Mode-level arbitration
17	 * (which producer is allowed to submit when) lives one layer up; the link
18	 * stays dumb. */
19	
20	void FretboardLink_Initialize(void);

13	static const uint8_t s_fret_bit[FRET_COUNT] =
14	{
15	    [FRET_GREEN]  = TIMING_BIT_GREEN,
16	    [FRET_RED]    = TIMING_BIT_RED,
17	    [FRET_YELLOW] = TIMING_BIT_YELLOW,
18	    [FRET_BLUE]   = TIMING_BIT_BLUE,
19	    [FRET_ORANGE] = TIMING_BIT_ORANGE,
20	};
21	
22	static volatile bool    s_enabled;
23	static volatile uint8_t s_fret_mask;
24	static volatile uint8_t s_strum_mask;
25	
26	static void recompute_and_send(void)
27	{
28	    if (!s_enabled) { return; }
29	    uint8_t mask = (uint8_t)(s_fret_mask | s_strum_mask);
30	    FretboardLink_Send(mask);
31	}
32	
33	void ManualControl_Initialize(void)
34	{
35	}
36	
37	bool ManualControl_IsEnabled(void)
38	{
39	    return s_enabled;
40	}
41	
42	void ManualControl_SetEnabled(bool enabled)
43	{
44	    if (enabled == s_enabled) { return; }
45	
46	    if (enabled)
47	    {
48	        /* Gate the pipeline before we own the wire so the next pipeline
49	         * frame can't race a stale mask onto the link between our zero
50	         * and our enable flip. */
51	        TimingPipeline_SetEnabled(false);
52	        s_fret_mask = 0u;
53	        s_strum_mask = 0u;
54	        s_enabled = true;
55	        FretboardLink_Send(0u);
56	        LOG_INFO("MC: manual mode on\r\n");
57	    }
58	    else
59	    {
60	        /* Release while we still own the wire, then hand back. The
61	         * pipeline's next advance() (≤ TP_TICK_MS = 5 ms) republishes
62	         * its own correct mask. */
63	        s_enabled = false;
64	        s_fret_mask = 0u;
65	        s_strum_mask = 0u;
66	        FretboardLink_Send(0u);
67	        TimingPipeline_SetEnabled(true);
68	        LOG_INFO("MC: manual mode off\r\n");
69	    }
70	}
71	
72	void ManualControl_SetFret(fret_t fret, bool pressed)
73	{
74	    if ((unsigned)fret >= FRET_COUNT) { return; }
75	    uint8_t bit = s_fret_bit[fret];
76	    if (pressed) { s_fret_mask |= bit; }
77	    else         { s_fret_mask &= (uint8_t)~bit; }
78	    recompute_and_send();
79	}
80	
81	void ManualControl_SetStrum(bool down, bool pressed)
82	{
83	    uint8_t bit = down ? TIMING_BIT_STRUM_DOWN : TIMING_BIT_STRUM_UP;
84	    if (pressed) { s_strum_mask |= bit; }
85	    else         { s_strum_mask &= (uint8_t)~bit; }
86	    recompute_and_send();
87	}

3	from __future__ import annotations
4

7	from .records import (
8	    Detector,
9	    Drop,
10	    Header,
11	    HDR_SIZE,
12	    PERF_LOG_HDR_MAGIC,
13	    RecordType,

15	    Stamp,

17	    STRIP_HDR_BYTES,
18	    STRIP_MAX_BYTES,
19	    Strip,
20	    TaskHighwater,
21	    TaskRuntime,
22	    Timing,
23	    UnknownRecord,
24	    _STRIP_BODY,

27	
28	Record = Union[
29	    Session, Stamp, Detector, Timing, Drop, TaskHighwater, TaskRuntime,
30	    Strip, UnknownRecord,
31	]
32	
33	
34	class DecodeError(Exception):
35	    pass
36	
37	
38	def _check(payload: bytes, expected_size: int, name: str) -> None:
39	    if len(payload) != expected_size:
40	        raise DecodeError(
41	            f"{name}: payload length {len(payload)} != expected {expected_size}"
42	        )
43	
44	
45	def _decode_session(hdr: Header, payload: bytes) -> Session:
46	    _check(payload, Session.SIZE, "Session")
47	    timer_freq_hz, schema_version, _reserved, fw_git_short, _reserved2 = (
48	        Session._BODY.unpack_from(payload, HDR_SIZE)
49	    )
50	    return Session(
51	        hdr=hdr,
52	        timer_freq_hz=timer_freq_hz,
53	        schema_version=schema_version,
54	        fw_git_short=fw_git_short,
55	    )
56	
57	
58	def _decode_stamp(hdr: Header, payload: bytes) -> Stamp:
59	    _check(payload, Stamp.SIZE, "Stamp")
60	    stage_id, _reserved, aux, _reserved2, _reserved3 = Stamp._BODY.unpack_from(
61	        payload, HDR_SIZE
62	    )
63	    return Stamp(hdr=hdr, stage_id=stage_id, aux=aux)
64	
65	
66	def _decode_detector(hdr: Header, payload: bytes) -> Detector:
67	    _check(payload, Detector.SIZE, "Detector")
68	    fields = Detector._BODY.unpack_from(payload, HDR_SIZE)
69	    hold = tuple(fields[0:5])
70	    edge = tuple(fields[5:10])
71	    pressed_mask = fields[10]
72	    edge_active_mask = fields[11]
73	    return Detector(
74	        hdr=hdr,
75	        hold_dist=hold,  # type: ignore[arg-type]
76	        edge_dist=edge,  # type: ignore[arg-type]
77	        pressed_mask=pressed_mask,
78	        edge_active_mask=edge_active_mask,
79	    )

110	    _check(payload, TaskHighwater.SIZE, "TaskHighwater")
111	    task_id, _reserved, words = TaskHighwater._BODY.unpack_from(payload, HDR_SIZE)
112	    return TaskHighwater(hdr=hdr, task_id=task_id, words=words)
113	
114	
115	def _decode_task_runtime(hdr: Header, payload: bytes) -> TaskRuntime:
116	    _check(payload, TaskRuntime.SIZE, "TaskRuntime")
117	    task_id, state, priority, _reserved, run_time_counter, _reserved2 = (
118	        TaskRuntime._BODY.unpack_from(payload, HDR_SIZE)
119	    )
120	    return TaskRuntime(
121	        hdr=hdr,
122	        task_id=task_id,
123	        state=state,
124	        priority=priority,
125	        run_time_counter=run_time_counter,
126	    )
127	
128	
129	def _decode_strip(hdr: Header, payload: bytes) -> Strip:
130	    if len(payload) < STRIP_HDR_BYTES:
131	        raise DecodeError(
132	            f"Strip: payload {len(payload)} < header {STRIP_HDR_BYTES}"
133	        )
134	    x, y, w, h, kind, _reserved = _STRIP_BODY.unpack_from(payload, HDR_SIZE)
135	    expected_pixels = w * h * STRIP_BPP
136	    if expected_pixels > STRIP_MAX_BYTES:
137	        raise DecodeError(
138	            f"Strip: w*h*bpp {expected_pixels} > max {STRIP_MAX_BYTES}"
139	        )
140	    expected_total = STRIP_HDR_BYTES + expected_pixels
141	    if len(payload) != expected_total:
142	        raise DecodeError(
143	            f"Strip: payload {len(payload)} != expected {expected_total} "
144	            f"({w}×{h}×{STRIP_BPP})"
145	        )
146	    bgr = bytes(payload[STRIP_HDR_BYTES:expected_total])
147	    return Strip(hdr=hdr, x=x, y=y, w=w, h=h, kind=kind, bgr=bgr)
148	
149	
150	_DISPATCH = {
151	    RecordType.SESSION: _decode_session,
152	    RecordType.STAMP: _decode_stamp,
153	    RecordType.DETECTOR: _decode_detector,
154	    RecordType.TIMING: _decode_timing,
155	    RecordType.DROP: _decode_drop,
156	    RecordType.TASK_HIGHWATER: _decode_task_highwater,
157	    RecordType.TASK_RUNTIME: _decode_task_runtime,
158	    RecordType.STRIP: _decode_strip,
159	}
160	
161	
162	def decode_record(payload: bytes) -> Record:
163	    """Decode an FCS-validated frame payload into a typed Record dataclass.
164	
165	    Caller (framing.iter_frames) has already verified FCS and length sanity.
166	    Unknown record types are surfaced as UnknownRecord so a forward-schema
167	    firmware does not crash an older host.
168	    """
169	    if len(payload) < HDR_SIZE:
170	        raise DecodeError(f"payload {len(payload)} < HDR_SIZE {HDR_SIZE}")
171	    hdr = Header.unpack(payload)
172	    if hdr.magic != PERF_LOG_HDR_MAGIC:
173	        raise DecodeError(f"bad magic 0x{hdr.magic:04x}")
174	
175	    decoder = _DISPATCH.get(hdr.type)
176	    if decoder is None:
177	        return UnknownRecord(hdr=hdr, raw=payload)
178	    return decoder(hdr, payload)
179
```
</details></tool-use>

42	void ManualControl_SetEnabled(bool enabled)
43	{
44	    if (enabled == s_enabled) { return; }
45	
46	    if (enabled)
47	    {
48	        /* Gate the pipeline before we own the wire so the next pipeline
49	         * frame can't race a stale mask onto the link between our zero
50	         * and our enable flip. */
51	        TimingPipeline_SetEnabled(false);
52	        s_fret_mask = 0u;
53	        s_strum_mask = 0u;
54	        s_enabled = true;
55	        FretboardLink_Send(0u);
56	        LOG_INFO("MC: manual mode on\r\n");
57	    }
58	    else
59	    {
60	        /* Release while we still own the wire, then hand back. The
61	         * pipeline's next advance() (≤ TP_TICK_MS = 5 ms) republishes
62	         * its own correct mask. */
63	        s_enabled = false;
64	        s_fret_mask = 0u;
65	        s_strum_mask = 0u;
66	        FretboardLink_Send(0u);
67	        TimingPipeline_SetEnabled(true);
68	        LOG_INFO("MC: manual mode off\r\n");
69	    }
70	}
71

73	{

# ─── Decode-time error paths ─────────────────────────────────────────────────


def test_bad_magic_raises() -> None:
    hdr = struct.pack("<HBBIQ", 0x1234, int(RecordType.SESSION), 0, 0, 0)
    payload = hdr + b"\x00" * 16
    with pytest.raises(DecodeError):
        decode_record(payload)


def test_truncated_payload_raises() -> None:
    with pytest.raises(DecodeError):
        decode_record(b"\x00" * (HDR_SIZE - 1))


def test_wrong_size_for_known_type_raises() -> None:
    # SESSION says 16-byte body; deliver a 4-byte body instead.
    hdr = build_header(RecordType.SESSION)
    with pytest.raises(DecodeError):
        decode_record(hdr + b"\x00" * 4)
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-06-01 17:19:54Z)**_

**On `xTaskGetIdleTaskHandle` via MCC:** good — that's the better path. Once you flip it in the FreeRTOS component, my `#undef`/`#define` override in [`FreeRTOSConfig.h`](firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/FreeRTOSConfig.h) becomes dead code (it'll re-define what MCC already emits as 1). I'll remove it and update the journal patch #8 entry once you confirm the MCC change is in. Or I can pre-emptively pull the override now — your call.

**On `xTaskGetHandle` for MCC tasks:** yes, this is exactly the right primitive if we want per-MCC-task breakdown instead of the OTHER aggregate. Mechanics:

```c
TaskHandle_t h = xTaskGetHandle("Legato");  // by name
if (h != NULL) { PerfLog_RegisterTaskForHighwater(PERF_TASK_LEGATO, h); }
```

What it buys: Legato, XLCDC, MAXTOUCH, SYS_INPUT, the USB host driver tasks each get their own row in the host RUNTIME table — same per-window CPU% computation, no schema change beyond extending `perf_task_id_t` and bumping `PL_TASK_SLOT_COUNT`.

**Tradeoffs to call out:**
- Requires `INCLUDE_xTaskGetHandle = 1` (another MCC knob, similar story).
- Task names are MCC-emitted strings — a regen could in theory rename one and the lookup silently returns NULL, falling back into OTHER. Worth a sanity check on the host (warn if a registered slot has zero runtime delta across many windows).
- Some MCC tasks are created at `vTaskStartScheduler` time, others at bus-enable / init-late (USB host). Registration has to happen after those points — easiest is a "register MCC tasks" call right after `PerfLog_Start` in app init, with NULL-tolerance per handle.
- Each named slot costs 1 enum entry + 1 byte on the wire per record. PL_RUNTIME_TASK_BUF is already 24 — should still cover us.

**Recommendation:** the OTHER aggregate is enough to *measure* whether MCC tasks are eating noticeable CPU. If OTHER turns out to be a few percent, the breakdown isn't urgent; if it's a big slice, identify the largest 2–3 by name and register those. Lazy-add by need.

Want me to (a) pull the FreeRTOSConfig.h idle override now since you'll handle it via MCC, (b) leave the OTHER-only design for v3 and revisit MCC-task naming if/when OTHER gets big, or both?
